'''''Jasminum angulare''''', the '''wild jasmine''' or '''angular jasmine''', is a species of [[flowering plant]] in the family [[Oleaceae]] that is indigenous to [[South Africa]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Jasminum angulare Vahl {{!}} Plants of the World Online {{!}} Kew Science |url=http://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:609325-1 |access-date=2023-03-26 |website=Plants of the World Online |language=en}}</ref>

This scrambling [[evergreen]] [[shrub]] can be grown in the sun or semi-shade. It has [[pinnation|pinnate]] leaves and masses of white, strongly-scented, star-shaped flowers which attract a variety of birds. This is one of around 10 species of jasmine that naturally occur in South Africa.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://indigenousplantfair.org.za/html/climbers.html |title=Climbers |access-date=2011-01-31 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120917220936/http://indigenousplantfair.org.za/html/climbers.html |archive-date=2012-09-17 |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=PlantZAfrica.com Homepage |url=http://www.plantzafrica.com/ |access-date=2023-03-26 |website=www.plantzafrica.com}}</ref>

It does not tolerate being frozen, so in temperate regions it is best grown under glass, in an unheated greenhouse or conservatory. In the [[UK]] it has gained the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]].<ref name = RHSPF>{{cite web 
| url= https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/9443/i-Jasminum-angulare-i/Details | title = RHS Plantfinder - ''Jasminum angulare''
| accessdate=14 March 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url= https://www.rhs.org.uk/plants/pdfs/agm-lists/agm-ornamentals.pdf 
| title = AGM Plants - Ornamental | date = July 2017 | page = 56 | publisher = Royal Horticultural Society | accessdate = 14 March 2018}}</ref>
